course_description:
This is the culminating professional experience course in the Master of Teaching (Secondary) program and as such the end point is for preservice teachers to have achieved the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers at a Graduate stage. Becoming a teacher requires commitment and dedication to both lifelong learning and personal autonomy. This 25-day block of professional experience demonstrates a movement along a developmental continuum where preservice teachers increasingly take on the roles and responsibilities of teachers to enter a phase of critical reflection and evaluation of their growth and development. This course focuses on the lifelong importance of professional learning to improve knowledge and practice and reinforces the critical need for ongoing engagement with colleagues, parents/carers and the community to build and foster supportive relationships.

As this course contains a professional experience component in a school, students are required to have a valid Blue Card for the duration of the placement.

This course has an approved course date variation from the standard semester schedule. Please visit the Course Date Variations page for further details.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate an understanding of schools as workplaces and be familiar with the statutory, ethical and other requirements that govern the work of teachers in schools.

Demonstrate the application of professional and disciplinary knowledge to engage with curriculum, pedagogy, assessment and reporting of student outcomes, and use this knowledge to design lesson plans and learning experiences.

Create inclusive, supportive and intellectually challenging educational environments that take account of challenging student behaviours, and demonstrate a range of teaching strategies that engage all learners and set appropriate learning goals for students of all abilities and from broad range of backgrounds.
Communicate effectively and confidentially with students, care givers and fellow professionals in a range of educational, social and cultural environments to support student engagement.
Demonstrate skills of critical reflection to evaluate student learning and assessment data and make informed decisions regarding student learning and required modifications to teaching practices.

Demonstrate skills of and purpose for critical reflection and engagement with APSTs, colleagues and mentors to identify professional learning needs and develop achievable plans for personal professional growth that will contribute to improved student learning, and effectively engage with constructive feedback through the stages of preservice teaching and beginning teaching.
Demonstrate clear, fluent, and coherent communication skills consistent with personal, professional and academic conventions.
Demonstrate all teaching and professional requirements of the professional experience placement.

assessment_details.task_description: Students are required to successfully complete 25 days of a supervised and assessed professional experience block placement in an approved school setting. The placement will be arranged only by the School of Education. The 25 day block will comprise of observations, planning and teaching full lessons and sequences of lessons. During the practicum, students are expected to demonstrate competence across the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APSTs). To do this, students will demonstrate that they have undertaken the inherent requirements of the role of a teacher. This means that students at the very least, will be expected to: Attend the school at least half an hour before and after school start and finish times to discuss that day's and subsequent days' expectations Attend any meetings held during the time of the practicum, e.g. departmental or whole of staff meetings or any professional development meetings where the school approves attendance. Participate in extracurricular activities, etc., available during the block. Students are expected to have read, and abide by the School of Education Policies and Procedures document for Professional Experience Placements. assessment_details.title: Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment (GTPA)
assessment_details.task_description: The Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment (GTPA) is an integrated assessment that connects the academic program and the professional experience, and in so doing connects research, theory and practice. The GTPA is a single culminating authentic summative assessment designed to demonstrate preservice teachers’ ability to meet the Graduate Teacher Standards and to plan, teach, assess and reflect on their final-year professional practice. The GTPA requires preservice teachers to demonstrate a capacity to interpret student data and modify and transform their teaching practices to improve student learning. This involves the preservice teacher in adapting and strategising teaching practices to meet the specific learning needs of students across the full range of abilities. The GTPA is assessed by teacher educators within higher education institutions (HEI). It complements but is separate from the Professional Experience Report. The GTPA task will be assessed by your workshop tutor at university. Refer to the “GTPA Preservice Teacher booklet" document for more information on the task. assessment_details.title: Applied professional practice: Simulation, critical reflection and graduate learning goals
assessment_details.category: Essay/ Critique, Reflection, Role play/ Simulation
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment focuses on developing critical reflection and professional learning goals as essential components of effective teaching practice. Drawing on 60 days of professional experience, students reflect on their evolving knowledge, skills, and teaching philosophy, informed by prior placements, supervising teacher feedback, and the Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment. You are required to complete Parts A – C as outlined below. You will be asked to identify five professional learning goals : Part A: One or two professional learning goals Part B and C: Three or four professional learning goals In Part A, you will be asked to review and annotate a previously developed unit plan from your GTPA submission, to explicitly incorporate the Personal and Social Capability (ACARA), supported by a 400-word critical reflection that justifies key adjustments and identifies relevant professional collaboration, culminating in one or two professional learning goals . Part B involves a simulated parent–teacher interview, where you will demonstrate effective, empathetic communication about a student’s learning, wellbeing, and inclusion, using your annotated unit plan. Note: The role play will not be directly assessed by your tutor. Instead, you will be asked to self-assess and critically evaluate your performance and demonstrate your understanding of effective communication with parents/carers through your written reflection in Part C. In Part C, you will produce a 500–600 word critical reflection evaluating your communication skills, use of data, engagement with parents/carers, and alignment with the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers. Across the task, you are required to engage with academic literature (8–10 references) to support analysis and synthesis. 1000 Words If you use AI and/or machine translation (MT) technologies in any way in the written component of this assessment task, you must provide specific details about how it was used. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute academic misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Guidelines about conventions for appropriate referencing and acknowledgement, including an example coversheet to provide details of use, are available here: Overview - AI tools for assignments - Library Guides at University of Queensland Library However, Part B of this assessment task is designed to protect academic integrity and assess your understanding of course concepts. You will be expected to complete a simulation exercise in the workshop where you complete a simulated parent-teacher interview with a peer and demonstrate your understanding and learning from Part A of the task, without the use of AI or other materials or tools. Use of prohibited materials in this section of the task may be investigated and treated as academic misconduct. Read full task description Hide full task description
